main.description: A word somebody decided to keep, from rite.mino.mobi/sharp. Usually a minted monosyllable — one syllable, English-shaped, and claimed by no dictionary — but a real word kept for its sound is the same record with `taken: true`. The point of putting it in the signer's own repo rather than in a table here: a shortlist of names you are thinking about is exactly the kind of small, personal, long-lived list that should not depend on one site continuing to exist, and /sharp stores none of it. The snapshot fields (`score`, `say`, `rhymes`, `domains`) are what the engine and the registries said AT THE MOMENT IT WAS KEPT — `domains` especially goes stale, because registrations change and a 404 was never a promise. Re-check before spending money.

word.description: The word itself, lowercase. Constrained to a length a domain label could hold, because that is usually why it was kept.

createdAt.description: When it was kept. Also the basis of the TID rkey, so a listRecords sweep comes back in the order they were kept.

syllables.description: Syllable count. From CMUdict when the word is real, from the heuristic in rite/sharp/engine.js when it is not.

taken.description: Was the word already an English word when it was kept? false for a minted one, true for a real one kept for its sound.

score.description: English-ness: the word's percentile against the log-probability of real English monosyllables under the phonotactic model. 50 is as ordinary as the median real monosyllable.

origin.description: Where it came from: 'mint' (procgen), 'real' (drawn from the corpus), or 'check' (typed into the checker).

style.description: The mint style that produced it — native, blunt, liquid, gnarly, old, bright, wide.

seed.description: The seed of the set it came out of. The minter is deterministic, so this plus the style reproduces the whole batch.

say.description: How it is pronounced. For a minted word this is a GUESS, assembled from real words spelled the same way — the onset's usual phones plus the rime's.

rhymes.description: Real English monosyllables sharing its phonetic rime — the evidence that an invented word still works in English.

homophones.description: Real words pronounced identically. A word can be unclaimed on the page and already taken in the ear.

domains.description: What the registries said, when they were asked. A SNAPSHOT, not a reservation.

domain.description: The full name asked about, e.g. lounce.dev.

verdict.description: free: the registry had no registration on file. taken: it did. unverifiable: the TLD is real but publishes no RDAP service, so nobody asked. unknown: the registry declined — rate limit, block or timeout. Only 'free' and 'taken' are answers, and 'free' means unregistered, never purchasable.

checkedAt.description: When the registry was asked. Registrations change; an old check is a rumour.
